limits.privacyFloor: 15-minute buckets under ~18 taps are suppressed in the source, so quiet hours are absent rather than zero; locations under 1500 taps a day are dropped.
limits.age: The shape is from 2020. The level is corrected to 2024-25 where the monthly feed names the station ('now'), and is null where it does not.
limits.notOccupancy: These are normalised shapes, not occupancies. scripts/train-occupancy-model.py turns them into a probability using measured Park&Ride occupancy.
limits.arrivalsNotTotalTaps: 'arrivals' is tap-OFFs only. Total taps peak at 7.30am in a commuter suburb, which is everyone leaving — reading that as visitors arriving puts a shopping strip's busiest hour at dawn.
limits.originOnly: 'parked' is present only where at least 62% of 6-10am taps are tap-ONs, i.e. a station people leave from. Elsewhere the cumulative net describes the evening exodus, not a kerb, so it is null and 'activity' is the signal.

calibration.note: Fitted against TfNSW Park&Ride occupancy, which is off-street. What transfers to a kerb is the response to commuter flow, not the level — so the runtime still caps its confidence. Only parkRideGain is taken from the fit: a commuter car park sits at a station, so it measures commuter flow well and neighbourhood arrivals badly, and the arrivals coefficient here comes out small and collinear with the clock. activityGain keeps its reasoned default until something kerbside can test it.
